svg.title: HybridGuard: associated observation surfaces and optional C1 relation
svg.desc: A cooperating Android app contains Native APIs and a WebView Host; App Web JavaScript is nested in the Host. Native-Web memory and timezone comparisons are integrated. Host-Web geometry is a standalone study outside Integrated App and its candidate pool. The dotted Native-Host link denotes shared context only. Schema counts are Native 84, Host 26, App Web 67 and external Browser 67; selected detectors use subsets. The external Browser is a separate Web execution; Chrome 133 and 134 identify the evaluated implementation. A thin leader enlarges the App Web record into the C1 panel, not an additional execution. Illustrative App Web and Browser timezone offsets are -480 and -540 minutes under UTC-minus-local. Both show field status observed and quality observed_value. C1 requires valid association and finite numeric non-Boolean offsets. The illustrated inequality yields T, the C1 condition outcome, not the whole detector result. Equal usable offsets yield F; unusable evidence yields U; invalid association yields FAILED. C1 has no timestamp gate. Connectors denote comparison, containment, or record excerpts, not inter-application communication, synchronized sampling, or attestation. No surface is trusted ground truth. Android, Chrome and WebView icons are official identity assets; technical symbols use Tabler Icons.

g.text: Equal → F · Unusable → U · Invalid link → FAILED

svg.text: Counts describe schemas, not selected inputs. No surface is trusted ground truth.
